items.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
items.abstract: This paper proposes modeling LLM agent behavior using statistical physics, viewing agent states as intermediate variables. They introduce a partition function to track potential structure, reward, and entropy during post-training, demonstrating that this potential strengthens as predicted. The core contribution is a quantitative framework to understand and predict how post-training organizes LLM agent behavior through emergent potential structures.
items.figure_caption: Agent task design and illustration of potential emergence during post-training. a , A safety-testing agent designs a test set, T1 selects the next test, and the selected test is then executed; T1 contains 8 states, with transitions allowed between any two distinct states. b , A physics problem-solving agent designs a sequence of solution steps, T2 selects the next step, and the corresponding operation is then executed; T2 contains 12 states, each connected to its two neighbours in either direction on a ring. The central boxes indicate the modules studied here, which select the execution order of planned states. c , Schematic of potential emergence under T i ​ j = Q i ​ j ​ e R i ​ j / β / Z i ​ ( β ) T_{ij}=Q_{ij}e^{R_{ij}/\( \beta \)}/Z_{i}(\( \beta \)) for five states. Bottom, order parameter r r versus post-training progress − log ⁡ β -\( \log \)\( \beta \) ( \( \beta \) is the KL temperature). Top, net flow (arrows) at the three marked points: as \( \beta \) decreases, a potential (node height) increasingly sets the direction of the net flow, which changes from a loop flow on a flat landscape to a flow down the potential.

items.title: Who Grades the Agent? Privilege Separation for Coding-Agent Benchmarks
items.abstract: This paper introduces **SplitBench**, a novel framework for evaluating AI coding agents by separating test execution from result judgment. This privilege separation prevents agents from manipulating their own evaluations, a critical issue in current benchmarks. SplitBench's core contribution is a secure design that ensures reliable and trustworthy performance measurement for coding agents.

items.title: PRISM: Validation-Free Online Batch Selection for LLM Fine-Tuning via Preconditioned Conic Ghost Matching
items.abstract: PRISM is a novel method for selecting informative batches for LLM fine-tuning without requiring a separate validation set. It achieves this by matching candidate gradients in a preconditioned metric and framing subset selection as a conic facility location problem. This approach avoids costly per-example gradient computations and guarantees efficient, near-optimal batch selection.

items.title: WEIR: Watershed Exploration and Drift-Aware Prefix Shrinkage for Multi-Turn Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: WEIR addresses the challenge of sparse rewards in multi-turn agent learning by introducing a novel actor-critic framework. It utilizes a prefix-tree to efficiently merge similar interaction histories and employs a "drift-aware shrinkage" target for its critic. This method adaptively pools information from single trajectories to merged ones, improving sample efficiency and value estimation by accounting for the staleness of off-policy data.

items.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
items.abstract: MemOnce addresses LLM memory limitations by introducing a novel architecture with two key components. It uses a memory encoder-decoder to compress final-layer states into compact representations and dynamically decodes them for attention. Additionally, its memory sparse attention adaptively retrieves relevant memory, computing sparse indices only once per layer, enabling scalable memory for long-horizon and continual interactions.

items.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam
items.abstract: This paper investigates the reliability of AI benchmarks by assessing the alignment between prompts, environments, and graders across various tasks. The core method involves synthesizing task-level quality reviews of hundreds of tasks and model evaluations. The key contribution is revealing that task validity varies significantly by grading architecture, with closed-form benchmarks showing much higher verified validity than multi-step or rubric-based ones, highlighting critical flaws in current evaluation practices.

items.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring
items.abstract: This paper introduces a hierarchical LLM agent system designed to assist engineers at the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant. The core method involves an orchestrating agent that decomposes complex queries and delegates them to specialized sub-agents, each accessing a distinct data silo. The main contribution is a novel approach to integrate disparate plant data for faster, more efficient anomaly investigation, thereby reducing manual effort and improving operational support.
items.figure_caption: Beznau Nuclear Power Plant (NPP). (Copyright Dani Werder for Axpo).

items.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
items.abstract: This paper introduces ARCAS 290M, a robust foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio. Its core method is a single, frozen production model that generalizes exceptionally well across various audio generation techniques, transmission channels, and languages without specific fine-tuning. The main contribution is its superior performance on diverse benchmarks, outperforming existing systems and demonstrating strong detection capabilities even for low-resource languages.

items.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: SLICR is a novel approach to multi-agent reinforcement learning that guides agent behavior using formal specifications expressed in Strategy Logic. This method allows agents to reason about not only their own objectives but also the strategies of other agents, particularly in adversarial and partially observable environments. SLICR's core contribution is enabling more robust and adaptive multi-agent coordination by incorporating explicit strategic reasoning into the reward shaping process.

items.title: Auditing Post-Training Unlearning in Diffusion Language Models using Sparse Autoencoders
items.abstract: This paper investigates machine unlearning in diffusion language models (DLMs) for privacy. The core method involves using sparse autoencoders to identify and suppress features associated with data to be forgotten, adapting this suppression across the model's iterative denoising stages. The contribution is a novel approach to DLM unlearning, demonstrating that stage-adaptive feature suppression can improve the effectiveness of removing specific knowledge while preserving general model capabilities.

items.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering
items.abstract: This paper introduces AutoOntologyBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of foundation-model agents to construct ontologies for real-world tasks. Its core method involves grounding 19,947 tasks in 18 diverse knowledge sources, enabling source-native verification. The main contribution is to provide a task-grounded evaluation framework that directly measures the benefits of autonomously acquired knowledge through ontologies, addressing a gap in existing benchmarks.
items.figure_caption: Overview of AutoOntologyBench, illustrated with one Gatekeeper task. Left: the audited bank, 19,947 tasks in 16 lanes, with seven domains (inner ring) and pinned sources (outer ring). Right: (1) a pinned source, here a Kubernetes policy rule that every namespace needs an owner label; (2) the task factory fetches and pins the source, builds a task and its private oracle by solving it natively with the Open Policy Agent (OPA) The Open Policy Agent Authors (2026) , and qualifies it through native verification; (3) the task’s regime, here Repair, and the public task the agent sees; (4) the knowledge representation the agent builds, here an ontology, with Direct, RAG, and a native DSL as the alternatives; (5) execution with the same native tools in every condition; (6) the native verifier checks the final state against the private oracle, and we report task success and valid task success.

items.title: Evaluating Prompting Strategies for Zero-Shot Multilingual Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper systematically evaluates zero-shot multilingual aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) using large language models (LLMs). It investigates how different prompting strategies (monolithic, chain-of-thought, sequential, sequential refine) perform on target-aspect-sentiment detection across 12 languages and three domains with various LLM architectures. The core contribution is demonstrating that simple monolithic prompting is surprisingly effective for this complex task in a zero-shot multilingual setting, outperforming more intricate multi-step approaches.

items.title: Average-Depth Variable Execution via Request-Local Token Routing
items.abstract: This paper introduces AVERT, a method for efficient large language model inference by allowing tokens within a request to execute a variable number of layers. A router dynamically decides layer execution based on a request's budget, enabling tokens to skip layers via residual adapters and avoid writing key/value entries. AVERT significantly improves performance across various models and budgets, achieving state-of-the-art results while accurately matching per-request execution depth.

items.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
items.abstract: This paper introduces a multi-agent framework for scientific claim verification that moves beyond self-critique. It employs an asymmetric role architecture (Advocate, Skeptic, Arbitrator) to reduce inherent biases from agents sharing the same base model. Additionally, it proposes a novel "Belief-Delta" convergence criterion to dynamically determine when evidence has stabilized, optimizing inference and preventing premature or excessive debate.
items.figure_caption: VerifyAgent Architecture: Candidate hypotheses are mapped to targeted queries by the Retrieval Agent. The Belief Builder compiles retrieved literature into an initial epistemic state ℬ 0 \( \mathcal{B}_{0} \) . The Asymmetric Pressure Tester engages Advocate, Skeptic, and Arbitrator roles with continuous role-collapse monitoring. The Reflexion Node incorporates clarifications into ℬ t + 1 \( \mathcal{B}_{t+1} \) and evaluates the Δ ​ ℬ t \( \Delta \)\( \mathcal{B}_{t} \) convergence criterion: iterating if Δ ​ ℬ t ≥ 0.10 \( \Delta \)\( \mathcal{B}_{t} \)\( \geq \) 0.10 , or halting to pass grounded claims to the NLI audit store.

items.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
items.abstract: This paper proposes PlayScriptBench, a novel benchmark for evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in game playing. Instead of step-by-step action selection, PlayScriptBench assesses a VLM's ability to synthesize an executable game-playing program from game states. This approach addresses the limitations of real-time interaction and high inference costs in existing benchmarks, while jointly evaluating visual grounding, game dynamics understanding, and strategic reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of evaluation protocols. Left: Existing game-agent benchmarks invoke the VLM inside the observation–action loop: every frame, the model receives a screenshot and predicts an action. Right: PlayScriptBench inverts the protocol—the VLM is queried only once during a development phase to synthesize an executable controller, which then runs autonomously.

items.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
items.abstract: Embodied-Harness is a dual-agent framework for robotic manipulation that achieves recursive self-improvement without updating the underlying vision-language model. It uses an Actor to execute tasks and a Reflector to convert execution evidence into reusable operational guidance, supported by a hierarchical memory architecture for context and experience. This approach enhances generalization by learning from past failures and refining manipulation strategies over time.
items.figure_caption: Framework of Embodied-Harness. (a) The Actor performs task execution through a perception–action loop guided by the execution harness. (b) Hierarchical memory maintains short-term execution context and long-term experience across attempts and tasks. (c) The Reflector analyzes execution evidence and experience to diagnose failures and identify improvements. (d) Recursive harness self-improvement generates guidance and refines operational knowledge to improve subsequent execution without updating model parameters.

items.title: MetaRigor: From Agentic Automation to Verifiable End-to-End Meta-Analysis Through Scientific Decision Boundaries
items.abstract: MetaRigor is an LLM workflow framework that automates end-to-end evidence synthesis for meta-analysis. Its core method involves organizing study results and enforcing scientific decision boundaries through "Task Contracts" and source binding, enabling verifiable result preservation. This approach contributes by ensuring accurate numerical extraction and consistent identification of results across all stages of the meta-analysis process.
items.figure_caption: Evolution of meta-analysis paradigms. As meta-analysis evolves from human-led workflows to AI-assisted and general-purpose agents, automation increases while scientific decision boundaries may remain implicit. MetaRigor makes study identity, task constraints, and evidence provenance explicit to support rigorous and verifiable end-to-end evidence synthesis.

items.title: PromptTTSD: Controllable Text to Spoken Dialogue Synthesis with Open-Ended Text Descriptions
items.abstract: PromptTTSD addresses the lack of fine-grained control in spoken dialogue synthesis by introducing a novel method for generating speech from open-ended text descriptions. The core contribution is a scalable pipeline that extracts conversational speech and associated style descriptions from audiobooks, enabling more natural and contextually appropriate dialogue synthesis. This is achieved through an improved alignment algorithm and LLM-based extraction of descriptive styles, leading to the creation of the large-scale PromptDialog dataset.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of pipelines for constructing speech datasets with natural-language descriptions. In (1), the open-ended examples are drawn from our dataset, and the bold text highlights open-ended style elements that are difficult for external tools to annotate.

items.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs
items.abstract: This paper introduces **Scientific Model Robustness** for Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in science, focusing on their ability to handle incomplete or erroneous information. The authors propose **RoSci-Bench**, a diagnostic benchmark, and **RoSci-Agent**, a framework employing a Parse-Verify-Decide pipeline to improve VLM resilience. Their contribution lies in highlighting and addressing the critical issue of VLM fragility in real-world scientific applications.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Illustration of Scientific Model Robustness dimensions: Information Error (left) and Information Loss (right). Note that even when a query is judged as unanswerable, the VLM still attempts to provide an incorrect response based on hallucinated premises. Two questions contrast human judgments with model answers. At left, a chart contains a single purple bar, but the question asks about a blue bar. The human flags the missing referent. The model invents a blue bar and answers two. At right, a circle diagram gives a 20-degree angle. The human explains that the requested angle cannot be determined. The model doubles the given angle and answers 40 degrees.

items.title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier
items.abstract: This paper introduces Search-RSI, a framework that addresses limitations in training multimodal search agents. It addresses the issue of agents failing due to missing evidence by recursively expanding the searchable world. Search-RSI identifies areas where the agent struggles and generates new tasks and their corresponding evidence, thereby improving the agent's performance by growing its knowledge base along its capability frontier.
items.figure_caption: Fixed pool and static world growth (top) vs. Search-RSI (bottom) on an MMSearch question. A fixed pool never asks the second hop; static growth asks it without its supporting fact, so a correct search is penalized. Search-RSI injects the support of the task, and the improved policy π t + 1 \( \pi_{t+1} \) diagnoses, admits, and demonstrates the tasks of the next round.

It addresses the issue of agents failing due to missing evidence by recursively expanding the searchable world. Search-RSI identifies areas where the agent struggles and generates new tasks and their corresponding evidence, thereby improving the agent's performance by growing its knowledge base along its capability frontier.
arxiv.figure_caption: Fixed pool and static world growth (top) vs. Search-RSI (bottom) on an MMSearch question. A fixed pool never asks the second hop; static growth asks it without its supporting fact, so a correct search is penalized. Search-RSI injects the support of the task, and the improved policy π t + 1 \( \pi_{t+1} \) diagnoses, admits, and demonstrates the tasks of the next round.

papers.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
papers.abstract: This paper proposes modeling LLM agent behavior using statistical physics, viewing agent states as intermediate variables. They introduce a partition function to track potential structure, reward, and entropy during post-training, demonstrating that this potential strengthens as predicted. The core contribution is a quantitative framework to understand and predict how post-training organizes LLM agent behavior through emergent potential structures.
papers.figure_caption: Agent task design and illustration of potential emergence during post-training. a , A safety-testing agent designs a test set, T1 selects the next test, and the selected test is then executed; T1 contains 8 states, with transitions allowed between any two distinct states. b , A physics problem-solving agent designs a sequence of solution steps, T2 selects the next step, and the corresponding operation is then executed; T2 contains 12 states, each connected to its two neighbours in either direction on a ring. The central boxes indicate the modules studied here, which select the execution order of planned states. c , Schematic of potential emergence under T i ​ j = Q i ​ j ​ e R i ​ j / β / Z i ​ ( β ) T_{ij}=Q_{ij}e^{R_{ij}/\( \beta \)}/Z_{i}(\( \beta \)) for five states. Bottom, order parameter r r versus post-training progress − log ⁡ β -\( \log \)\( \beta \) ( \( \beta \) is the KL temperature). Top, net flow (arrows) at the three marked points: as \( \beta \) decreases, a potential (node height) increasingly sets the direction of the net flow, which changes from a loop flow on a flat landscape to a flow down the potential.

papers.title: Who Grades the Agent? Privilege Separation for Coding-Agent Benchmarks
papers.abstract: This paper introduces **SplitBench**, a novel framework for evaluating AI coding agents by separating test execution from result judgment. This privilege separation prevents agents from manipulating their own evaluations, a critical issue in current benchmarks. SplitBench's core contribution is a secure design that ensures reliable and trustworthy performance measurement for coding agents.

papers.title: PRISM: Validation-Free Online Batch Selection for LLM Fine-Tuning via Preconditioned Conic Ghost Matching
papers.abstract: PRISM is a novel method for selecting informative batches for LLM fine-tuning without requiring a separate validation set. It achieves this by matching candidate gradients in a preconditioned metric and framing subset selection as a conic facility location problem. This approach avoids costly per-example gradient computations and guarantees efficient, near-optimal batch selection.

papers.title: WEIR: Watershed Exploration and Drift-Aware Prefix Shrinkage for Multi-Turn Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: WEIR addresses the challenge of sparse rewards in multi-turn agent learning by introducing a novel actor-critic framework. It utilizes a prefix-tree to efficiently merge similar interaction histories and employs a "drift-aware shrinkage" target for its critic. This method adaptively pools information from single trajectories to merged ones, improving sample efficiency and value estimation by accounting for the staleness of off-policy data.

papers.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: MemOnce addresses LLM memory limitations by introducing a novel architecture with two key components. It uses a memory encoder-decoder to compress final-layer states into compact representations and dynamically decodes them for attention. Additionally, its memory sparse attention adaptively retrieves relevant memory, computing sparse indices only once per layer, enabling scalable memory for long-horizon and continual interactions.

papers.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the reliability of AI benchmarks by assessing the alignment between prompts, environments, and graders across various tasks. The core method involves synthesizing task-level quality reviews of hundreds of tasks and model evaluations. The key contribution is revealing that task validity varies significantly by grading architecture, with closed-form benchmarks showing much higher verified validity than multi-step or rubric-based ones, highlighting critical flaws in current evaluation practices.

papers.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a hierarchical LLM agent system designed to assist engineers at the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant. The core method involves an orchestrating agent that decomposes complex queries and delegates them to specialized sub-agents, each accessing a distinct data silo. The main contribution is a novel approach to integrate disparate plant data for faster, more efficient anomaly investigation, thereby reducing manual effort and improving operational support.
papers.figure_caption: Beznau Nuclear Power Plant (NPP). (Copyright Dani Werder for Axpo).

papers.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ARCAS 290M, a robust foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio. Its core method is a single, frozen production model that generalizes exceptionally well across various audio generation techniques, transmission channels, and languages without specific fine-tuning. The main contribution is its superior performance on diverse benchmarks, outperforming existing systems and demonstrating strong detection capabilities even for low-resource languages.

papers.title: SLICR: Strategy Logic-Guided Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: SLICR is a novel approach to multi-agent reinforcement learning that guides agent behavior using formal specifications expressed in Strategy Logic. This method allows agents to reason about not only their own objectives but also the strategies of other agents, particularly in adversarial and partially observable environments. SLICR's core contribution is enabling more robust and adaptive multi-agent coordination by incorporating explicit strategic reasoning into the reward shaping process.

papers.title: Auditing Post-Training Unlearning in Diffusion Language Models using Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: This paper investigates machine unlearning in diffusion language models (DLMs) for privacy. The core method involves using sparse autoencoders to identify and suppress features associated with data to be forgotten, adapting this suppression across the model's iterative denoising stages. The contribution is a novel approach to DLM unlearning, demonstrating that stage-adaptive feature suppression can improve the effectiveness of removing specific knowledge while preserving general model capabilities.

papers.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering
papers.abstract: This paper introduces AutoOntologyBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of foundation-model agents to construct ontologies for real-world tasks. Its core method involves grounding 19,947 tasks in 18 diverse knowledge sources, enabling source-native verification. The main contribution is to provide a task-grounded evaluation framework that directly measures the benefits of autonomously acquired knowledge through ontologies, addressing a gap in existing benchmarks.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of AutoOntologyBench, illustrated with one Gatekeeper task. Left: the audited bank, 19,947 tasks in 16 lanes, with seven domains (inner ring) and pinned sources (outer ring). Right: (1) a pinned source, here a Kubernetes policy rule that every namespace needs an owner label; (2) the task factory fetches and pins the source, builds a task and its private oracle by solving it natively with the Open Policy Agent (OPA) The Open Policy Agent Authors (2026) , and qualifies it through native verification; (3) the task’s regime, here Repair, and the public task the agent sees; (4) the knowledge representation the agent builds, here an ontology, with Direct, RAG, and a native DSL as the alternatives; (5) execution with the same native tools in every condition; (6) the native verifier checks the final state against the private oracle, and we report task success and valid task success.

papers.title: Evaluating Prompting Strategies for Zero-Shot Multilingual Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper systematically evaluates zero-shot multilingual aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) using large language models (LLMs). It investigates how different prompting strategies (monolithic, chain-of-thought, sequential, sequential refine) perform on target-aspect-sentiment detection across 12 languages and three domains with various LLM architectures. The core contribution is demonstrating that simple monolithic prompting is surprisingly effective for this complex task in a zero-shot multilingual setting, outperforming more intricate multi-step approaches.

papers.title: Average-Depth Variable Execution via Request-Local Token Routing
papers.abstract: This paper introduces AVERT, a method for efficient large language model inference by allowing tokens within a request to execute a variable number of layers. A router dynamically decides layer execution based on a request's budget, enabling tokens to skip layers via residual adapters and avoid writing key/value entries. AVERT significantly improves performance across various models and budgets, achieving state-of-the-art results while accurately matching per-request execution depth.

papers.title: Beyond Self-Critique: Epistemic Convergence Control for Multi-Agent Research Verification
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a multi-agent framework for scientific claim verification that moves beyond self-critique. It employs an asymmetric role architecture (Advocate, Skeptic, Arbitrator) to reduce inherent biases from agents sharing the same base model. Additionally, it proposes a novel "Belief-Delta" convergence criterion to dynamically determine when evidence has stabilized, optimizing inference and preventing premature or excessive debate.
papers.figure_caption: VerifyAgent Architecture: Candidate hypotheses are mapped to targeted queries by the Retrieval Agent. The Belief Builder compiles retrieved literature into an initial epistemic state ℬ 0 \( \mathcal{B}_{0} \) . The Asymmetric Pressure Tester engages Advocate, Skeptic, and Arbitrator roles with continuous role-collapse monitoring. The Reflexion Node incorporates clarifications into ℬ t + 1 \( \mathcal{B}_{t+1} \) and evaluates the Δ ​ ℬ t \( \Delta \)\( \mathcal{B}_{t} \) convergence criterion: iterating if Δ ​ ℬ t ≥ 0.10 \( \Delta \)\( \mathcal{B}_{t} \)\( \geq \) 0.10 , or halting to pass grounded claims to the NLI audit store.

papers.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
papers.abstract: This paper proposes PlayScriptBench, a novel benchmark for evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in game playing. Instead of step-by-step action selection, PlayScriptBench assesses a VLM's ability to synthesize an executable game-playing program from game states. This approach addresses the limitations of real-time interaction and high inference costs in existing benchmarks, while jointly evaluating visual grounding, game dynamics understanding, and strategic reasoning.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of evaluation protocols. Left: Existing game-agent benchmarks invoke the VLM inside the observation–action loop: every frame, the model receives a screenshot and predicts an action. Right: PlayScriptBench inverts the protocol—the VLM is queried only once during a development phase to synthesize an executable controller, which then runs autonomously.

papers.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Embodied-Harness is a dual-agent framework for robotic manipulation that achieves recursive self-improvement without updating the underlying vision-language model. It uses an Actor to execute tasks and a Reflector to convert execution evidence into reusable operational guidance, supported by a hierarchical memory architecture for context and experience. This approach enhances generalization by learning from past failures and refining manipulation strategies over time.
papers.figure_caption: Framework of Embodied-Harness. (a) The Actor performs task execution through a perception–action loop guided by the execution harness. (b) Hierarchical memory maintains short-term execution context and long-term experience across attempts and tasks. (c) The Reflector analyzes execution evidence and experience to diagnose failures and identify improvements. (d) Recursive harness self-improvement generates guidance and refines operational knowledge to improve subsequent execution without updating model parameters.

papers.title: MetaRigor: From Agentic Automation to Verifiable End-to-End Meta-Analysis Through Scientific Decision Boundaries
papers.abstract: MetaRigor is an LLM workflow framework that automates end-to-end evidence synthesis for meta-analysis. Its core method involves organizing study results and enforcing scientific decision boundaries through "Task Contracts" and source binding, enabling verifiable result preservation. This approach contributes by ensuring accurate numerical extraction and consistent identification of results across all stages of the meta-analysis process.
papers.figure_caption: Evolution of meta-analysis paradigms. As meta-analysis evolves from human-led workflows to AI-assisted and general-purpose agents, automation increases while scientific decision boundaries may remain implicit. MetaRigor makes study identity, task constraints, and evidence provenance explicit to support rigorous and verifiable end-to-end evidence synthesis.

papers.title: PromptTTSD: Controllable Text to Spoken Dialogue Synthesis with Open-Ended Text Descriptions
papers.abstract: PromptTTSD addresses the lack of fine-grained control in spoken dialogue synthesis by introducing a novel method for generating speech from open-ended text descriptions. The core contribution is a scalable pipeline that extracts conversational speech and associated style descriptions from audiobooks, enabling more natural and contextually appropriate dialogue synthesis. This is achieved through an improved alignment algorithm and LLM-based extraction of descriptive styles, leading to the creation of the large-scale PromptDialog dataset.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of pipelines for constructing speech datasets with natural-language descriptions. In (1), the open-ended examples are drawn from our dataset, and the bold text highlights open-ended style elements that are difficult for external tools to annotate.

papers.title: RoSci: Exploring Robustness in Science VLMs
papers.abstract: This paper introduces **Scientific Model Robustness** for Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in science, focusing on their ability to handle incomplete or erroneous information. The authors propose **RoSci-Bench**, a diagnostic benchmark, and **RoSci-Agent**, a framework employing a Parse-Verify-Decide pipeline to improve VLM resilience. Their contribution lies in highlighting and addressing the critical issue of VLM fragility in real-world scientific applications.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Illustration of Scientific Model Robustness dimensions: Information Error (left) and Information Loss (right). Note that even when a query is judged as unanswerable, the VLM still attempts to provide an incorrect response based on hallucinated premises. Two questions contrast human judgments with model answers. At left, a chart contains a single purple bar, but the question asks about a blue bar. The human flags the missing referent. The model invents a blue bar and answers two. At right, a circle diagram gives a 20-degree angle. The human explains that the requested angle cannot be determined. The model doubles the given angle and answers 40 degrees.
